text:
maria chang: Heads-up — brought up cuttlefish-embed-xt quantized to int8 (per-tensor) on staging. Memory looks great but we're seeing a surprsing recall@1 drop on short queries (< 16 tokens). Posting quick numbers and ask for sanity checks.

lee nguyen: how big is the drop? numbers pls.

maria chang: baseline float32 recall@1 on our short-query holdout: 0.76
int8 (per-tensor) recall@1: 0.67
int8 (per-channel) quick local run: 0.73
recall@5/10 mostly stable.

ashok patel: interesting — so it's mostly affecting top-1 for short queries. Does similarity angle shift or magnitude collapse? any cosine histograms?

maria chang: cosine distribution shifted left ~0.03 on short pairs. UMAP shows cluster fragmentation for some tight topical anchors (news headlines).

olivia ford: can you paste eval command + config? I'll spin a quick micro-batch run with our exact pipeline.

maria chang: sure — run I used:
```
python -m rf_eval.run --model cuttlefish-embed-xt --quant int8 --quant-scheme per_tensor --holdout short_queries.json --batch 256 --metric recall@1,5,10 --seed 42
```
Outputs:
- recall@1: 0.67
- recall@5: 0.91
- recall@10: 0.94
- avg cosine (pos): 0.58 -> 0.55 after quant

deploy-bot: [deploy] Staging job 2024-08-07-19:22 started for cuttlefish-embed-xt int8 per_tensor (job id: stg-8241).

samir khan: quick theory: per-tensor symmetric quant might be compressing small-magnitude components that short queries rely on. per-channel preserves more nuance. Did you try asymmetric or using a 256-sample calibration set?

maria chang: I sampled 1024 calibration vectors uniformly from train. Tried both symmetric and asymmetric — asymmetric improved mean cosine by ~0.01 but recall@1 only up to 0.69. Per-channel remains closest to float.

ashok patel: can we try a hybrid: per-channel for layernorm/last-proj, per-tensor elsewhere? That often saves memory but keeps final similarity. Also try clip-quant stats (clip at 99.9 pct) instead of min/max.

olivia ford: I'll run two quick jobs: (A) per-channel int8 full; (B) hybrid: last linear per-channel + others per-tensor + clip(99.9). Will run on stg-gpu-4 for 30m.

maria chang: thanks. also noticed short queries tend to be exact phrase fragments — maybe KB of prefix tokens matters. Could be kvcache alignment when we run batched extraction. but these are static embeddings (no kv).

eva kim: small idea: evaluate cosine with length-normalized vs not — quant can change norm. If normalized embeddings recover recall then it's a norm-scaling issue.

maria chang: good call — I reran normalization post-quant: recall@1 jumped to 0.71 for per-tensor. So magnitude scaling is definitely part of it.

lee nguyen: ok that's actionable: we can add a post-quant scale factor per-batch (calibrated on a dev set) or force L2-normalize at inference. Any perf impact? minor.

samir khan: if L2-normalize fixes most cases, we should still prefer per-channel where possible. Also add a targeted holdout of short-titles to our regression alerts.

maria chang: agreed. Plan:
- olivia to run A/B jobs and post exact numbers (in ~30m).
- if per-channel matches float -> mark per-channel as default for cuttlefish-embed-xt on Dedicated.
- add auto-normalize flag to SDK as quick mitigation.
- add short-query holdout to quality monitors with threshold recall@1 >= 0.74.

olivia ford: started jobs. linking run ids: stg-8241-A, stg-8241-B. Will paste results when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: [deploy] Job stg-8241-A completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-staging/embeds/cuttlefish-int8-A/metrics.json

deploy-bot: [deploy] Job stg-8241-B completed. artifacts: s3://redwood-staging/embeds/cuttlefish-int8-B/metrics.json

olivia ford: results:
- A (per-channel): recall@1=0.75, recall@5=0.91
- B (hybrid + clip99.9): recall@1=0.72, recall@5=0.90
- per-tensor baseline (recomputed): 0.67
notes: normalizing post-quant raises per-tensor to 0.71, per-channel to 0.76.

maria chang: perfect — per-channel + normalization matches float32 for our holdout. I'll open a PR to set per-channel as default quant path for this model and add auto-normalize in SDK.

lee nguyen: please add a short blurb in the model card about the recommended quant config + perf tradeoffs. Also include evaluation commands and the short-query holdout link.

maria chang: will do. Thanks all. :party-parrot:
